angle: Brevo's homepage tells the story of a rebrand paying off — measured by when 'Why Brevo?' disappeared from the nav. The article tracks the specific homepage signals that mark each phase: explanation → brand-recall → category ownership.
distinct_from: rebrand patience measured by nav signal
LTV outcome H1 vs aspiration H1
h1: Brevo Homepage Teardown: How a Rebranded Company Stopped Explaining Itself and Started Owning a Category

sections.goal: Open with the Sendinblue → Brevo rebrand context and the single homepage signal that shows the rebrand succeeded: the removal of 'Why Brevo?' from navigation. Name the period, the H1 shift, and what the reader will be able to test on their own post-rebrand homepage.

sections.custom_h2: ## Brevo's homepage arc 2023–2026: from rebrand introduction to customer-lifetime-value platform
sections.goal: Show three distinct phases: (1) Jan 2023 — new brand introducing itself with 'Why Brevo?' and 'Get Brevo' CTA; (2) mid-period evidence of brand settling (if available); (3) 2026 — category ownership mode with LTV H1 and demo CTA. Anchor to page title and CTA evidence.

sections.custom_h2: ## How Brevo's homepage messaging shifted from brand introduction to lifetime customer ownership
sections.goal: Analyze the H1 shift ('Connections that spark growth' → 'Turn Every Email SMS Order Interaction into a Lifetime Customer') and the meta description hedge removal ('and more' → full product list). Explain what each change signals about the visitor's assumed awareness level.

sections.custom_h2: ## How Brevo's CTAs and navigation changed the sales motion
sections.goal: Analyze: (1) CTA shift from 'Get Brevo'/'Why Brevo?' (brand-building) to 'Sign up free'/'Get a demo' (action-oriented); (2) nav rename 'Products' → 'Platform'; (3) addition of channel nav items (Wallet, Phone). End with a test about nav item names.

sections.custom_h2: ## Why Brevo renamed itself and then rewrote its entire homepage
sections.goal: Explain the Sendinblue brand equity problem, the 2023 competitive context (Klaviyo IPO, HubSpot expansion, Mailchimp/Intuit), and why 'customer engagement platform' was the right category to claim. End with the timeline implication: 2–3 years from rebrand to category ownership.

sections.custom_h2: ## What SaaS teams can study from Brevo's homepage evolution
sections.goal: 3 patterns: (1) 'Why [Company]?' removal as a measurable brand-recall milestone; (2) replacing meta-description hedges with a full product list; (3) omnichannel H1 as a category claim. Each must end with a specific test the reader can run.
